review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

6:1.sourceText: Τολμᾷ τις ὑμῶν πρᾶγμα ἔχων πρὸς τὸν ἕτερον κρίνεσθαι ἐπὶ τῶν ἀδίκων, καὶ οὐχὶ ἐπὶ τῶν ἁγίων;
6:1.targetText: If any of you has a grievance against another, how dare he go to law before the unrighteous instead of before the saints!

groups.note: The question Τολμᾷ ("does he dare") is rendered as the exclamation how dare he.
The participle ἔχων ("having") is recast as the condition If … has.
καὶ οὐχί ("and not") is rendered instead of.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:2.sourceText: ἢ οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ ἅγιοι τὸν κόσμον κρινοῦσιν; καὶ εἰ ἐν ὑμῖν κρίνεται ὁ κόσμος, ἀνάξιοί ἐστε κριτηρίων ἐλαχίστων;
6:2.targetText: Do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if you are to judge the world, are you not competent to judge trivial cases?

groups.note: ἐν ὑμῖν ("by you") becomes the subject of BSB's active wording.
The passive κρίνεται ("is judged") is recast as active: you are to judge.
ἀνάξιοι ("unworthy") is rendered not competent.
κριτηρίων ("of courts, of cases") is rendered to judge … cases.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ἤ ("or") unexpressed before the question.

6:3.sourceText: οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ἀγγέλους κρινοῦμεν, μήτιγε βιωτικά;
6:3.targetText: Do you not know that we will judge angels? How much more the things of this life!

6:4.sourceText: βιωτικὰ μὲν οὖν κριτήρια ἐὰν ἔχητε, τοὺς ἐξουθενημένους ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ, τούτους καθίζετε;
6:4.targetText: So if you need to settle everyday matters, do you appoint as judges those of no standing in the church?

groups.note: κριτήρια ("courts, lawsuits") is rendered to settle … matters.
ἔχητε ("you have", that is, lawsuits) is rendered you need.
τοὺς ἐξουθενημένους ("those despised") is rendered of no standing; the resumptive τούτους carries those.
καθίζετε ("do you seat") is rendered do you appoint.

unmappedSource.reason: μέν has no separate counterpart; BSB renders μὲν οὖν with So alone.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB adds as judges to name the role; the Greek has no word for judges.

6:5.sourceText: πρὸς ἐντροπὴν ὑμῖν λέγω. οὕτως οὐκ ἔνι ἐν ὑμῖν οὐδεὶς σοφὸς, ὃς δυνήσεται διακρῖναι ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ;
6:5.targetText: I say this to your shame. Is there really no one among you wise enough to arbitrate between his brothers?

groups.note: ὑμῖν ("for you") is rendered your.
οὕτως ("so, thus") is rendered really.
The double negative οὐκ … οὐδείς is rendered by the one English negative no one.
ὃς δυνήσεται ("who will be able") is rendered enough, before to arbitrate.
ἀνὰ μέσον ("in the middle of") is rendered between.
The singular ἀδελφοῦ ("brother") is rendered brothers after between.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB supplies the object this; the Greek has no word for it.

6:6.sourceText: ἀλλὰ ἀδελφὸς μετὰ ἀδελφοῦ κρίνεται, καὶ τοῦτο ἐπὶ ἀπίστων;
6:6.targetText: Instead, one brother goes to law against another, and this in front of unbelievers!

groups.note: ἀδελφοῦ ("brother") is rendered another, avoiding the repetition.

6:7.sourceText: ἤδη μὲν οὖν ὅλως ἥττημα ὑμῖν ἐστιν ὅτι κρίματα ἔχετε μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν. διὰ τί οὐχὶ μᾶλλον ἀδικεῖσθε; διὰ τί οὐχὶ μᾶλλον ἀποστερεῖσθε;
6:7.targetText: The very fact that you have lawsuits among you means that you are thoroughly defeated already. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be cheated?

groups.note: The noun ἥττημα ("defeat") is rendered as the verb are defeated.
ἐστιν ("is"), which equates the fact with a defeat, is rendered means.
ὅτι ("that") introduces the subject clause, rendered The fact that.
διὰ τί ("for what reason") is rendered Why.
διὰ τί ("for what reason") is rendered Why.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves μὲν οὖν ("so then, indeed") unexpressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds that to introduce the clause after means.
English adds very for emphasis; the Greek has no word for it.

6:8.sourceText: ἀλλὰ ὑμεῖς ἀδικεῖτε καὶ ἀποστερεῖτε, καὶ τοῦτο ἀδελφούς.
6:8.targetText: Instead, you yourselves cheat and do wrong, even against your own brothers!

groups.note: καὶ τοῦτο ("and this", and that too) is rendered even.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB adds the possessive your own for emphasis; the Greek has no pronoun.

6:9.sourceText: ἢ οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ἄδικοι Θεοῦ βασιλείαν οὐ κληρονομήσουσιν; μὴ πλανᾶσθε· οὔτε πόρνοι οὔτε εἰδωλολάτραι οὔτε μοιχοὶ οὔτε μαλακοὶ οὔτε ἀρσενοκοῖται
6:9.targetText: Do you not know that the wicked will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: Neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor men who submit to or perform homosexual acts,

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ἤ ("or") unexpressed before the question.

6:10.sourceText: οὔτε κλέπται οὔτε πλεονέκται, οὐ μέθυσοι, οὐ λοίδοροι, οὐχ ἅρπαγες βασιλείαν Θεοῦ κληρονομήσουσιν.
6:10.targetText: nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor verbal abusers, nor swindlers, will inherit the kingdom of God.

6:11.sourceText: καὶ ταῦτά τινες ἦτε· ἀλλὰ ἀπελούσασθε, ἀλλὰ ἡγιάσθητε, ἀλλὰ ἐδικαιώθητε ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἐν τῷ Πνεύματι τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν.
6:11.targetText: And that is what some of you were. But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified, in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God.

groups.note: ταῦτα ("these things") is rendered by the cleft that is what.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not repeat but before this clause.
BSB does not repeat but before this clause.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English uses a cleft sentence; the Greek says simply "these things you were".

6:12.sourceText: Πάντα μοι ἔξεστιν, ἀλλ’ οὐ πάντα συμφέρει. πάντα μοι ἔξεστιν, ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐγὼ ἐξουσιασθήσομαι ὑπό τινος.
6:12.targetText: “Everything is permissible for me,” but not everything is beneficial. “Everything is permissible for me,” but I will not be mastered by anything.

6:13.sourceText: τὰ βρώματα τῇ κοιλίᾳ, καὶ ἡ κοιλία τοῖς βρώμασιν· ὁ δὲ Θεὸς καὶ ταύτην καὶ ταῦτα καταργήσει. τὸ δὲ σῶμα οὐ τῇ πορνείᾳ ἀλλὰ τῷ Κυρίῳ, καὶ ὁ Κύριος τῷ σώματι·
6:13.targetText: “Food for the stomach and the stomach for food,” but God will destroy them both. The body is not intended for sexual immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.

groups.note: καὶ … καί ("both … and") is rendered both.
ταύτην ("this", the stomach) and ταῦτα ("these", the foods) are rendered together as them.

6:14.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Θεὸς καὶ τὸν Κύριον ἤγειρεν καὶ ἡμᾶς ἐξεγερεῖ διὰ τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ.
6:14.targetText: By His power God raised the Lord from the dead, and He will raise us also.

groups.note: ἤγειρεν ("raised") is rendered raised … from the dead.
The second καί of καὶ … καί ("both … and") is rendered and … also.

6:15.sourceText: οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι τὰ σώματα ὑμῶν μέλη Χριστοῦ ἐστιν; ἄρας οὖν τὰ μέλη τοῦ Χριστοῦ ποιήσω πόρνης μέλη; μὴ γένοιτο.
6:15.targetText: Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and unite them with a prostitute? Never!

groups.note: ποιήσω … μέλη ("shall I make … members") is rendered shall I unite.
πόρνης ("of a prostitute") is rendered with a prostitute after unite.
μὴ γένοιτο ("may it never be") is the fixed formula of rejection, rendered Never.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English and joins the participle ἄρας ("taking") to the main verb; the Greek has no καί here.

6:16.sourceText: ἢ οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ὁ κολλώμενος τῇ πόρνῃ ἓν σῶμά ἐστιν; Ἔσονται γάρ, φησίν, οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν.
6:16.targetText: Or don’t you know that he who unites himself with a prostitute is one with her in body? For it is said, “The two will become one flesh.”

groups.note: The contraction carries the negative οὐκ.
ἔσονται εἰς ("will be into") is a Semitic idiom for "will become".
φησίν ("he says", that is, Scripture says) is rendered it is said.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB adds with her to make the union explicit; the Greek has no words for it.

6:17.sourceText: ὁ δὲ κολλώμενος τῷ Κυρίῳ ἓν πνεῦμά ἐστιν.
6:17.targetText: But he who unites himself with the Lord is one with Him in spirit.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB adds with Him to make the union explicit; the Greek has no words for it.

6:18.sourceText: φεύγετε τὴν πορνείαν. πᾶν ἁμάρτημα ὃ ἐὰν ποιήσῃ ἄνθρωπος ἐκτὸς τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν· ὁ δὲ πορνεύων εἰς τὸ ἴδιον σῶμα ἁμαρτάνει.
6:18.targetText: Flee from sexual immorality. Every other sin a man can commit is outside his body, but he who sins sexually sins against his own body.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB uses a contact clause (a man can commit), so the relative ὃ ἐάν ("whatever") has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB adds other to set this sin apart from sexual immorality; the Greek has no word for it.

6:19.sourceText: ἢ οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι τὸ σῶμα ὑμῶν ναὸς τοῦ ἐν ὑμῖν Ἁγίου Πνεύματός ἐστιν, οὗ ἔχετε ἀπὸ Θεοῦ; καὶ οὐκ ἐστὲ ἑαυτῶν;
6:19.targetText: Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have received from God? You are not your own;

groups.note: ἔχετε ("you have") is rendered you have received, with from God.
